changes: NEW — section11.net: a small static website with a landing page, Getting started, the four sync/export setup guides and report examples. Pages are built from the repository Markdown, so the repo stays the source of truth. Includes search titles and descriptions, a sitemap, and a robots.txt that allows all crawlers.

RELIABILITY (v11.68 / v3.133 / push.py v0.6) — every direct HTTP request now has a timeout; safe reads retry only eligible failures, with bounded backoff and Retry-After. push.py writes report applied, not_applied or unknown and are never blindly retried; exit code 2 means the change may or may not have landed. recent_activities[] now sets chat_notes_status: "unavailable" when activity messages could not be retrieved, so unavailable is no longer confused with no notes.

HISTORY REFRESH (v11.70 / v3.137) — history.json no longer waits for a Sunday/Monday window; an outdated history refreshes on the first eligible sync. A failed fetch keeps the last good history instead of replacing it with an empty or degraded one, and failed refreshes back off after 1 h, 6 h and then 24 h. On GitHub Actions, automatic refreshes run on every 16th workflow run; Sync Now bypasses only that budget.

GITHUB SYNC — the default workflow checks every 30 minutes (:07 and :37 UTC), with Sync Now to request a manual refresh. Scheduled and manual runs share one queue, publication fails closed and is verified after ambiguous pushes, and manual runs provide a short-lived training-data ZIP. Existing data-repo workflow copies do not update automatically; merge the new template and keep your own schedule.

WORKOUT SUMMARIES (v3.136) — planned-workout summaries no longer invent recovery intent, silently drop steps or flatten repeats; an unsafe summary is withheld rather than guessed. Optional step text such as Recovery can make intent explicit but is not required.

SOURCE AUTHORITY (v11.69) — example files are renamed *.example.json, and anything under examples/json-examples/ is fictional reference data that must never be used for coaching or as a fallback. Stable athlete facts come from the current official dossier and training metrics from current JSON. Troubleshooting now covers the four delivery paths (filesystem, connector, upload, URL) and their freshness, and ChatGPT and Gemini setup guidance is updated.

INSTALL + UPDATE (v3.138) — --init now installs exactly the files --update manages, after checking paths and hashes. Maintainer folders (.github, dev) are no longer distributed; older installs can move them aside through an interactive prompt that requires the word move. Nothing is deleted.
PUSH.PY v0.7 — Intervals.icu athlete IDs are accepted exactly as shown: i-prefixed IDs, digits-only IDs from early accounts, or 0 for the API key owner.

ZERO VALUES (v3.139) — activity decoupling, average temperature and wind speed now keep a real 0 instead of showing it as missing. Fields where 0 means no sensor or no data (power, heart rate, cadence, speed, work, calories) still read as null.

DOCS + TOOLING — new FIT File & Merger reference architecture (documentation only); Workout Reference template examples in examples/agentic aligned with the library (AE-1 is steady endurance, recovery is AE-4); GitHub Actions usage figures labelled as estimates; new developer test harness for sync.py and push.py.

Upgrade: local users can run python3 section11/examples/sync.py --update. Replacing sync.py changes script_hash and clears cached history, intervals and routes, so expect one heavier rebuild over the next syncs. If you copied PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS_WEB.md or PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS_AGENTIC.md, re-copy the block. Renamed example files are listed as orphans after updating; removing them needs a separate confirmation.
